page: Microsoft Azure E96bds_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance configured with 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity totals 672.0 GB, delivering 7.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance bundles 3,865 GB of local solid-state drive (SSD) storage for fast scratch space and high-speed temporary caching, while operating without discrete hardware GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks highlight significant capabilities in multi-threaded computation, memory bandwidth, and cryptographic execution. The instance scores in the top 25 percent for stress-ng multi-core tests, PassMark overall CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside top-decile performance in PassMark encryption routines supported by AES-NI and VAES instruction sets. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 331.15 GB/sec, complemented by strong throughput in database operations and Redis SET benchmarks exceeding 88 million operations per second.

Single-threaded tasks register average results, reflecting the standard 2.8 GHz base clock speed of the Intel platform. Furthermore, text generation with large language models exhibits weak throughput in the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. With substantial memory density and multi-core scalability, the E96bds_v5 provides qualitative resource efficiency for large enterprise database deployments, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, large-scale ETL pipelines, and concurrent software build infrastructure.
description: Microsoft Azure E96bds_v5 is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor, delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores on the x86_64 architecture. It includes 672.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB per vCPU, along with 3,865 GB of local SSD storage and no integrated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top quartile for multi-core computation, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and memory throughput, alongside top-tier cryptographic performance driven by hardware AES and VAES instruction flags. Single-thread operations and large language model text generation perform at moderate to lower tiers due to reliance on CPU execution rather than hardware acceleration. The high memory ratio, solid multi-threaded performance, and abundant local disk space make the E96bds_v5 suitable for running enterprise relational databases, distributed in-memory caching clusters, large-scale compilation tasks, and multi-threaded data processing workloads.
